# codelaw

> The linter and formatter for code written by people and by AI: one Rust engine, rules as Markdown files, for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, JSON, YAML, TOML, Markdown, CSS (and SCSS) and HTML. 651 rules in 17 packs, plus 23 engine rules; every rule has a fix (`auto`, `suggest` or `manual`). Installed as `codelaw` from npm or PyPI.

Generated by `scripts/rule-docs.py` from the rule files; CI fails when it is stale. Configuration lives in `codelaw.toml`: `extends` a preset to turn rules on, `[rules]` to set a severity or options. `codelaw explain <rule>` prints any rule's fix steps offline.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arpitarya/codelaw/main/README.md): what codelaw is, the packs, getting started
- [Usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arpitarya/codelaw/main/USAGE.md): commands, configuration, agent wiring
- [Rule reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arpitarya/codelaw/main/docs/rules/README.md): the index of every rule page, and the configuration forms
- [Every rule in one file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arpitarya/codelaw/main/docs/rules/llms-full.txt): what each rule checks, its options, how to fix it, its examples
- [Rule catalogue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arpitarya/codelaw/main/docs/rules/rules.json): JSON — id, packs, languages, fix kind, options schema, presets, fix steps, one don't/do example
